native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: The Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) phases are characterized by strongly negative scores along the first principal component (PC1) in a PCA of prehistoric forms of capital. PC1 represents a macro-historical axis separating a non-metal lithic/amber/ceramic Neolithic regime (negative loadings: pottery form diversity, flint axes/celts, amber) from a metallurgical prestige/hoard Bronze Age regime (positive loadings: copper/gold, pottery decoration, depots/hoards, swords/hatchets, daggers). Middle Neolithic exhibits a deeply negative trajectory (mean -1.430, trough -1.848 at 3200 BCE) reflecting peak amber and pottery form diversity with zero metallurgy. The Younger Neolithic maintains consistently negative PC1 scores (mean -1.177, range -1.621 to -0.645) dominated by peak axes/celts and monument count, remaining entirely distinct from later metal-rich periods.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Cleaned and parsed capital.csv (39 century time slices from 4300 to 500 BCE) and time_series_data.csv (37 slices from 4100 to 500 BCE). 2. Conducted Principal Component Analysis (SVD) on the 12 standardized indicators of symbolic, social, cultural, and economic capital. 3. Evaluated PC1 explained variance (31.84% for 39 slices, 34.63% for 37 slices) and component loadings across all forms of capital. 4. Computed summary statistics (mean, std, median, min, max) and individual century trajectory scores for Middle Neolithic (MN, 3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (SG, 2900-2300 BCE). 5. Conducted sensitivity checks across standardized vs centered covariance matrices and 39 vs 37 century time windows.
